primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: X-linked hypophosphatemia due to PHEX loss of function
mechanism: PHEX loss of function increases FGF23 activity. Excess FGF23 reduces proximal-tubular phosphate reabsorption by promoting internalization of sodium-phosphate cotransporters and also lowers calcitriol synthesis, producing chronic phosphate wasting and defective bone mineralization.
vignette: A 6-year-old boy has progressive bowing of the legs, short stature, bone pain, and recurrent dental abscesses. Serum phosphate is low with renal phosphate wasting; serum calcium is normal. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in PHEX.
lead: Which of the following downstream changes most directly causes this patient's renal phosphate wasting?
correct: FGF23-mediated internalization of proximal-tubular sodium-phosphate cotransporters
distractors: Excess parathyroid hormone causing internalization of proximal-tubular sodium-phosphate cotransporters
Loss of the SLC34A3 sodium-phosphate cotransporter reducing proximal-tubular phosphate uptake
Reduced intestinal phosphate absorption caused by loss of the vitamin D receptor
Generalized proximal-tubule dysfunction causing urinary glucose and amino-acid loss
distractor_notes: PTH excess can produce renal phosphate wasting by reducing proximal-tubular sodium-phosphate transport, but this patient has genetically confirmed PHEX-related XLH in which excess FGF23 is the operative signal.
SLC34A3 loss causes hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets with hypercalciuria by directly reducing NaPi-IIc transport; it is a distinct genetic cause from PHEX-mediated FGF23 excess.
Vitamin D receptor loss causes hereditary vitamin D-resistant rickets through impaired vitamin-D signaling and intestinal mineral absorption, not the PHEX/FGF23 renal phosphate-wasting mechanism.
Fanconi syndrome causes generalized proximal-tubule losses including glucose and amino acids; XLH causes a selective FGF23-mediated phosphate-wasting phenotype.
key_expl: PHEX loss of function leads to excess FGF23. FGF23 acts on the proximal tubule to internalize sodium-phosphate cotransporters, decreasing phosphate reabsorption and causing phosphaturia. It also reduces calcitriol synthesis. Chronic hypophosphatemia impairs skeletal and dental mineralization.
objective: Connect PHEX deficiency with excess FGF23 and proximal-tubular sodium-phosphate cotransporter internalization in X-linked hypophosphatemia.
